hardware_label: Measured on 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-13420H (laptop-1e); not a Raspberry Pi, not embedded hardware
profile_claim: One efficiency core (Gracemont, 3.4 GHz) of the development laptop: slow-core proxy, not embedded hardware.

verdicts.question: Did the pipeline meet the 100 ms deadline?
verdicts.statement: No. 18.7 % of 888 frames missed 100 ms. Median latency 91 ms is 0.9x the deadline; P99 is 125 ms.
verdicts.rule: pass: 0 violations; warn: 0 < violations <= 5 %; fail: violations > 5 %. Violation = per-frame pipeline latency (preprocess + register) strictly greater than the deadline.

verdicts.question: Did registration produce valid matches?
verdicts.statement: 297 of 299 registrations passed the validity gate (99.3 %); rejections: {'high_residual': 2}.
verdicts.rule: pass: >= 99 % accepted; warn: >= 90 %; fail: < 90 %. Accepted = passes the registration validity gate.

verdicts.question: How accurate was the estimated trajectory?
verdicts.statement: ATE RMSE 0.89 m (max 1.79 m) over 34.5 m of ground-truth path after rigid alignment; position RPE is reported per window in the summary. Both include any unmodelled sensor-to-body offset (lever arm) between the estimate and the ground-truth body frame, so they mix drift with extrinsic bias. Scan-to-scan odometry has no loop closure, so error accumulates with distance.
verdicts.rule: descriptive; no pass/fail threshold is applied to accuracy

verdicts.question: Does this result describe the OS1-64?
verdicts.statement: No. This dataset uses a different sensor (Ouster OS0-128 Rev C (128 beams, 1024 columns, 90 deg vertical FOV, 10 Hz)); do not read it as an OS1-64 result.
